title: Cardiovascular Burden of Primary Hyperparathyroidism: Associations with Risk Profile, Cardiac Structure, and Function
content: Background/Objectives: Primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) has been increasingly linked to cardiovascular morbidity, but whether cardiovascular alterations reflect dis-ease-specific effects or conventional risk factors remains uncertain. This study aimed to identify clinical, biochemical, electrocardiographic (ECG), and echocardiographic factors associated with cardiovascular abnormalities in PHPT. Methods: In this single-center cross-sectional case–control study, 5,868 hospitalized patients were screened between 01 January 2024 and 31 December 2025. Fifty-four patients with biochemically confirmed PHPT and 23 age- and sex-matched controls underwent standardized clinical, laboratory, ECG, and transthoracic echocardiographic assessment. Results: Patients with PHPT had higher systolic blood pressure than controls (median 132.5 vs. 130.0 mmHg; p = 0.049), a higher prevalence of type 2 diabetes (18.5% vs. 0.0%; p = 0.028), more frequent left ventricular hypertrophy (57.4% vs. 30.4%; p = 0.046), longer transmitral flow deceleration time (median 281.5 vs. 222.0 ms; p < 0.001), higher pulmonary artery systolic pressure (median 24.5 vs. 19.0 mmHg; p < 0.001), and more frequent aortic valve fibrosis (38.9% vs. 13.0%; p = 0.032). All PHPT patients were classified as high or very high cardiovascular risk, compared with 87.0% of controls (p = 0.008). In adjusted models, PHPT remained independently associated with longer transmitral flow deceleration time, higher pul-monary artery systolic pressure, aortic valve fibrosis, and pericardial effusion. Conclusions: PHPT is associated with higher cardiovascular burden and selected echocardio-graphic abnormalities beyond traditional risk factors, supporting systematic cardiovas-cular assessment in these patients.
